USMEvaluation class

Source: R/usm_evaluation.R
USMEvaluation.Rd

The USMEvaluation class detects USMs (situations) where the model performance on a given variable is very degraded compared to a reference version, relative to the overall performance of the species on that variable.

Details

For each variable and each USM, the following ratio is computed:

$$RMSE\_ratio = 100 \times \frac{RMSE_{eval} - RMSE_{ref}}{RMSE_{species}}$$

where:

  • RMSE_eval: RMSE of the evaluated version, for the variable, on that USM.

  • RMSE_ref: RMSE of the reference version, for the variable, on that USM.

  • RMSE_species: RMSE of the evaluated version, for the variable, computed on the whole species (all USMs together).

A USM is considered as not passing the test if, for at least one variable:

  • RMSE_ratio > ratio_threshold (default 50%), OR

  • more than max_degraded_vars (default 3) variables have RMSE_ratio > degraded_threshold (default 20%) on that USM.

USMs/variables with less than 10 observations (n_obs) are ignored, consistently with RRmseComparison/DeterioratedUSMComparison.

The class can be used in two ways:

  • Driven by a Configuration + workspace, like SpeciesEvaluation: create with config (and optionally workspace/backend/logger), then call run().

  • Manually, by directly providing stats_usm and stats_species (or a pre-computed data) for a single species, useful for unit testing.

Active bindings

degraded_vars

Data frame of variable/USM combinations (across all species) where rmse_ratio exceeds degraded_threshold (default 20%).

critical_vars

Data frame of variable/USM combinations (across all species) where rmse_ratio exceeds ratio_threshold (default 50%).

failed_usms

Data frame with columns species/situation for USMs that do not pass the test: either at least one variable with a ratio above ratio_threshold, or more than max_degraded_vars variables above degraded_threshold.

success

TRUE if the USM evaluation is successful, i.e. no USM failed the test for any species.

is_empty

TRUE if there is no data to evaluate.

USMEvaluation$new()

Create a new USMEvaluation object.

Usage

USMEvaluation$new(
  config = NULL,
  workspace = NULL,
  backend = NULL,
  logger = default_logger,
  ratio_threshold = 50,
  degraded_threshold = 20,
  max_degraded_vars = 3,
  species = NULL,
  stats_usm = NULL,
  stats_species = NULL,
  data = NULL
)

Arguments

config

A Configuration object containing the necessary parameters for the evaluation (same as SpeciesEvaluation). Required to use run().

workspace

An optional EvalWorkspace object. If not provided, a new EvalWorkspace will be created using the provided configuration.

backend

An optional ParallelBackend object for parallel processing. If not provided, a new ParallelBackend will be created using the provided configuration.

logger

An optional logger object for logging messages. If not provided, the default logger will be used.

ratio_threshold

Numeric threshold (%) above which a single variable makes the USM fail. Default 50.

degraded_threshold

Numeric threshold (%) above which a variable is considered degraded. Default 20.

max_degraded_vars

Maximum number of degraded variables (ratio > degraded_threshold) tolerated per USM before it is considered failed. Default 3 (i.e. fails starting at 4 degraded variables).

species

Optional species name, used in manual mode (ignored if config is provided).

stats_usm

Manual mode: data frame of per-USM stats (RMSE, n_obs), for evaluated and reference groups, e.g. as returned by CroPlotR's summary method with all_situations = FALSE, stats = c("RMSE", "n_obs").

stats_species

Manual mode: data frame of species-level stats (RMSE), e.g. as returned by CroPlotR's summary method with all_situations = TRUE (default).

data

Manual mode: optional pre-computed data frame (bypasses stats_usm/stats_species computation).

USMEvaluation$run()

Run the USM evaluation. This method computes, for each species found in the workspace (filtered according to the configuration), the RMSE_ratio per variable and per USM, and stores the results internally.

Usage

USMEvaluation$run()

USMEvaluation$get_data()

Return the underlying data frame (one row per variable/USM/species combination, with columns: species, situation, variable, rmse_eval, rmse_ref, rmse_species, ratio, n_obs).

Usage

USMEvaluation$get_data()

USMEvaluation$export()

Export the USM evaluation data for deteriorated USMs to a CSV file.

The exported file is written to the configured output directory and is named Deteriorated_USM.csv. Only USMs that contain evaluation data are included in the export.

Usage

USMEvaluation$export()

USMEvaluation$summary()

Print a summary of the USM evaluation results, species by species.

Usage

USMEvaluation$summary()

deep

Whether to make a deep clone.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Driven by config/workspace, like SpeciesEvaluation
config <- list(
  eval_workspace = "path/to/eval_workspace",
  usms = c("USM1", "USM2"),
  species = c("Species1", "Species2"),
  var2exclude = c("var1", "var2"),
  parallel = TRUE,
  cores = 4,
  output_dir = "path/to/output"
)
usm_eval <- USMEvaluation$new(config = config)
usm_eval$run()
usm_eval$summary()
usm_eval$get_data()
usm_eval$failed_usms

# Manual mode (unit tests)
usm_eval <- USMEvaluation$new(
  species = "Species1",
  stats_usm = stats_usm,
  stats_species = stats_species
)
usm_eval$summary()
} # }
